title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the continuation (pp. 650bis-787) of La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois. There Grothendieck studies (ρ,σ)-groups: profinite groups generated by an element ρ of order 3 and an element σ of order 2, of the type of the completion of PSL2(Z) ≅ Z/3 * Z/2. They contain the fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,∞}, with generators λ0, λ1, λ∞, as a normal subgroup. They also contain an orientation-reversing element τ. The aim is to describe a 'Teichmüller/Galois' symmetry group Z_{ρ,σ} of such a group. Up to conventions, this is a precursor of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group.

Previous page. It sets up a dictionary between two kinds of objects.
- On one side: a discrete group extension 1 → M → E → H → 1, with M a finite free Z-module and H a finite discrete group.
- On the other side: a group scheme 𝔈 over Spec Z, with neutral component the vector group M̲ = V(M) and finite étale component group H.
- For any S, the 'diagonal' part 𝔈^Δ(S) is an extension of H by Γ(S, O_S ⊗ M).
- Taking A = Ẑ gives 𝔈^Δ(Ẑ) ≅ the profinite completion E^∧.

This page, step by step.
1. Grothendieck announces that he will make explicit, for Ĝ and G· → Ĝ, the general constructions of §49 VI. He takes the distinguished normal subgroup to be 𝔊^q := M̲ = 𝔊°, the neutral component.
2. In the present case 𝔊^q is exactly the closed subgroup of the (ρ,σ)-group generated by λ0, λ1, λ∞. So it is the geometric π1 of the thrice-punctured line, here abelian, i.e. a metabelian-type truncation.
3. He decides to work 'in the schematic framework rather than the profinite one'. This means group schemes over Z with vector-group neutral component; the profinite objects are recovered as Ẑ-points.
4. The key step is the group Z_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(𝔊^+). It consists of the automorphisms u satisfying three conditions:
   - (a) u(ρ) is locally conjugate to ρ by some α ∈ 𝔊^q_τ = {1,τ}·M̲, where conjugation by τ is allowed and gives a sign ε;
   - (b) the same for σ, with some β;
   - (c) u preserves the inertia subgroup L0 at the cusp 0, equivalently L0^{Π0};
   - (d) u preserves 𝔊^q; this is automatic.
   The 'existence' in (a) and (b) is meant locally, in the fpqc/étale sense, as the margin note says.
5. Parametrisation. Such u is determined by u(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ησ, with ξ, η ∈ ΓΠ. Here Π ⊃ M̲ has index 2.
6. The next page gives the conditions on (ξ,η):
   - local conjugacy;
   - an 'equation of centres' ξ = η ℓ1^ν, with ν ∈ Ĝa and μ = 2ν+1 a unit. This is the analogue of Drinfeld's λ = 2m+1 ∈ Ẑ^*;
   - signs ε3(u), ε2(u) read off from whether α, β involve τ.

Purpose. The page computes a GT-type group as automorphisms of a (ρ,σ)-group that respect the conjugacy classes of torsion and the cusp inertia. This is done in a finite-type, abelian-kernel, group-scheme truncation over Spec Z, as a 'provisional version'.
errors: Not a mathematical error, but a gap: the group in condition (b) ('∃β ∈ ......') is left blank. Presumably it is again 𝔊^q_τ = {1,τ}·M̲, as in (a).
Claim (d) is said to be 'automatic' without proof. It is plausible, since 𝔊^q = 𝔊° is characteristic as the neutral component, but it relies on u being an automorphism of group schemes.
The notation for Π (Π = M ⋊ ... ?) is unclear and partly crossed out. Only 'M of index 2 in Π' is reliable.
Possible conflation of the notation 𝔊_{ρ,σ} (profinite) with its schematic version. Grothendieck himself flags that he will later need to distinguish 𝔊_{ρ,σ} from 𝔊^q_{ρ,σ}.

ideas.what: Defining a Teichmüller/Galois symmetry group as automorphisms of a (ρ,σ)-group (completion of PSL2(Z)-type groups) that send ρ and σ to conjugates (up to the orientation element τ) and preserve the cusp inertia L0
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group via automorphisms of \hat{PSL2(Z)} / \hat{B3} respecting torsion conjugacy classes and inertia
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990, GT); Ihara; Lochak–Schneps and Harbater–Schneps / Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1990s) for automorphism-group characterisations
ideas.where_published: Theme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The main part of La Longue Marche discusses (ρ,σ)-groups; this specific definition (15) is unsure

ideas.what: Parametrising u by u(ρ) = ξρ, u(σ) = ησ, with an 'equation of centres' ξ = η ℓ1^ν, μ = 2ν+1 invertible
ideas.modern_name: Analogue of Drinfeld's parameters (λ, f), with λ = 2m+1 ∈ Ẑ^*

ideas.what: Working with group schemes over Spec Z whose neutral component is a vector group V(M) and whose component group is finite. These are attached to discrete extensions with abelian kernel, and recover the profinite completion as Ẑ-points (𝔈^Δ(Ẑ) ≅ E^∧)
ideas.modern_name: Schematic/algebraic hull of an abelian-by-finite group; a forerunner of unipotent/relative completions over Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Relative/unipotent completion: Deligne, Hain (over Q). Abelian-by-finite schematic hulls over Z: no standard credit

ideas.what: Conjugacy conditions imposed only locally (fppf/étale-local existence of α, β), with signs ε2, ε3 recording conjugation by τ
ideas.modern_name: Locally inner / class-preserving automorphisms of group schemes; orientation character

missed.claim: A 'schematic' (group-scheme over Spec Z) version of the GT-type group Z_{ρ,σ} is defined. It is built at the level of a (ρ,σ)-group whose fundamental-group part is abelian (a vector group). It is preferred explicitly to the profinite version, which is recovered by Ẑ-points. The literature has profinite GT and pro-unipotent GT over Q (Drinfeld), and metabelian/abelianised GT quotients studied profinitely (Ihara). I know of no integral group-scheme version of such truncations.
missed.quote: Nous ferons cependant les constructions dans le cadre schématique, plutôt que profini
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would interpolate between profinite GT (Ẑ-points) and pro-unipotent GT over Q (Q-points) in one object over Z, at least for metabelian-type truncations. That is a theme of current interest: integral and motivic GT, and p-adic comparisons.

missed.claim: The definition of Z_{ρ,σ} through conjugacy of the torsion generators ρ, σ (allowing the twist by τ) plus preservation of cusp inertia L0, rather than through Drinfeld's equations, is close to the later characterisations of GT. It is a 'provisional version' and could be compared with Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps type results.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents an independent, earlier Grothendieck route to GT via automorphisms of (ρ,σ)-groups, relevant to the history and to the variants with complex conjugation (τ, the signs ε).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working definition of a GT-like automorphism group, close in spirit to known GT characterisations; the λ = 2m+1 analogue and the conjugacy conditions are familiar. The mildly notable point is the explicit choice of an integral group-scheme framework for abelian-kernel truncations, which seems absent from the literature. But it is only set up here, not carried out.
transcription_corrections: Title reads 'Le groupe Z̃_{ρ,σ} : version provisoire' (tilde over Z).
'en y/prenant' is a correction to 'en y prenant'.
In (16), 'Π = M^{ue}' is doubtful; the image shows 'Π = M' followed by a crossed-out symbol (possibly a semidirect-product sign), with '(M ss-gr. d'indice 2 dans Π)' below.
In (15b), 'β ∈ ......' is genuinely left blank by Grothendieck, not illegible.

The passage 'on a déjà pu dire les relations ... il n'y a pas [?] contiguïté — d'introduire la relation q' is largely illegible; a plausible reading is 'on a les premiers ... dans les relations ... pas contiguïté — d'introduire la relation q'.
The left-margin note probably reads 'Je pourrais à la fin donner les constructions profinies [comme] variantes ... des [constructions] schématiques' (tentative).
